title_en: Xinda Company Shijiazhuang Office v. China-Arab Company et al. — dispute over a loan guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: A guaranty contract is the result of a meeting of minds between the parties. Any change of the guarantor must be consented to by the creditor. If the creditor and the guarantor have not formed an agreement to discharge the guaranty liability, even if the debtor or a third party provides alternative security for the creditor and the creditor accepts it, the guarantor's guaranty liability cannot be discharged thereby.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over loan guaranty contract; second instance trial; Supreme People's Court; Hebei Province; legal person; financial institution; Guaranty Law; whether change of guarantor requires creditor's consent; whether provision of new security discharges original guarantor's liability; reversal; loan contract; guaranty letter; letter of commitment; assignment of creditor's rights; party autonomy; contract dispute; security; guaranty; Ah Company et al. loan guaranty contract dispute
full_text_en:
Xinda Company Shijiazhuang Office
v.
China-Arab Fertilizer Co., Ltd. et al.
— Dispute over loan and guaranty contract

【Ruling Summary】

A guaranty contract is the result of mutual agreement between the parties, and any change of the guarantor requires the consent of the creditor. If there is no agreement between the creditor and the guarantor to extinguish the guaranty obligation, even if the debtor or a third party provides additional corresponding security to the creditor and the creditor accepts it, the guarantor's guaranty obligation shall not be exempted on that ground.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 200

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): China Xinda Asset Management Corporation Shijiazhuang Office. Domicile: Wanlong Building, No. 30 South Ping'an Street, Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province.
Responsible person: Zhang Guoying, Director of the Office.
Agent ad litem: An Hongmin, lawyer of Hebei Jili Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Liu Aiqiang, lawyer of Hebei Jili Law Firm.

Appellee (defendant at first instance): China-Arab Fertilizer Co., Ltd. Domicile: Eastern Section of Jianshe Street, Haigang District, Qinhuangdao City, Hebei Province.
Legal representative: Chen Lihua, Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Wang Qinghua, lawyer of Hebei Jimin Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Lu Chunxiu, lawyer of Beijing Zhenghe Law Firm.

Defendant at first instance: Hebei Jizhou Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Factory. Domicile: No. 14 South Nanqiao Street, Jizhou City, Hebei Province.
Legal representative: Wang Lihu, Factory Director.
Agent ad litem: Zhou Shihao, lawyer of Hebei Jizhou Shuangji Law Firm.

The appellant, China Xinda Asset Management Corporation Shijiazhuang Office (hereinafter referred to as Xinda Shiban), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2005) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 2 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court in the case of dispute over loan and guaranty contract with the appellee, China-Arab Fertilizer Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhonga Company), and the defendant at first instance, Hebei Jizhou Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Factory (hereinafter referred to as Jizhou Zhongyi). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Wu Qingbao as presiding judge, and acting judges Gong Bangyou and Liu Min as members. Court clerk Zhao Suijun served as recorder. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

On October 20, 1993, Jizhou Zhongyi entered into a foreign exchange loan contract with China Construction Bank Hebei Branch (hereinafter referred to as the Provincial Construction Bank), stipulating: the loan amount was USD 1.82 million, the purpose was investment in the project of Hebei Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hebei Zhongyi), the loan term was from October 20, 1993, to June 30, 1997, the interest rate was a floating rate, repayment was to commence on December 31, 1995, and was to be made in three installments. Zhonga Company issued an Irrevocable Foreign Exchange Guaranty Letter to the Provincial Construction Bank for this loan, which stated: "This guaranty letter guarantees the repayment of all or part of the matured principal and interest under Loan Contract No. 93008 that the borrower fails to repay on time, and agrees to repay the overdue principal, interest, and expenses of the borrower within fourteen days after receiving the Bank's written notice. This guaranty letter shall take effect from the date of issuance and shall automatically expire upon full repayment of all principal, interest, and expenses owed by the borrower." After the loan guaranty contract was signed, the Provincial Construction Bank disbursed the loan in accordance with the contract. This loan was invested in Hebei Zhongyi as Jizhou Zhongyi's capital contribution.

On November 25, 1995, Hebei Zhongyi issued a Letter of Undertaking to the Provincial Construction Bank, stating: "Hebei Jixian Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Factory borrowed USD 1.82 million from your Bank on October 20, 1993, under Loan Contract No. 93008. For this reason, our company hereby solemnly undertakes: our company shall bear joint and several repayment liability for the repayment of the principal and interest of this loan, and waive all rights of defense. This letter of undertaking is a supplement to Loan Contract No. 93008 and has the same legal effect."

After the loan matured, neither the borrower nor the guarantor repaid it. The Provincial Construction Bank made demands for repayment. On July 8, 1998, Yue Hongjun, the legal representative of Jizhou Zhongyi, signed and confirmed the notice of overdue loan repayment issued by the Provincial Construction Bank. On November 16, 1999, the Provincial Construction Bank issued a notice of assignment of creditor's rights to Jizhou Zhongyi, and Jizhou Zhongyi affixed its official seal on the receipt of the notice, with its legal representative Yue Hongjun signing. On December 3, 1999, the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban entered into an Agreement on Assignment of Creditor's Rights, stipulating: the Provincial Construction Bank assigned to Xinda Shiban its creditor's rights against the borrower Jizhou Zhongyi as of September 20, 1999, including the principal of the loan of USD 1.82 million, on-balance-sheet accrued interest of USD 375,110.75, and collection interest of USD 36,627,401. On December 21, 1999, the Provincial Construction Bank issued a Notice of Assignment of Security Rights (Jian Ji Wai No. 4) to Hebei Zhongyi, and Hebei Zhongyi signed and affixed its seal on the receipt. On December 1, 2000, Xinda Shiban demanded repayment from the borrower Jizhou Zhongyi and Hebei Zhongyi. On October 22, 2002, Xinda Shiban made a demand for repayment from Zhonga Company by notarization. On November 19, 2004, Xinda Shiban published an announcement of assignment, demand, and sale of creditor's rights in the Hebei Economic Daily, which included Jizhou Zhongyi and Zhonga Company. On November 23, 2004, Xinda Shiban and the Provincial Construction Bank jointly published an announcement of assignment and demand of creditor's rights in the Hebei Economic Daily, which included Jizhou Zhongyi and Zhonga Company. On November 30, 2004, Xinda Shiban filed a lawsuit, requesting an order that Jizhou Zhongyi repay the principal and interest of the loan and that Zhonga Company bear the guaranty liability.

It was also found that:

In March 1992, Hebei Zhongyi (Party A) and Jixian Finance Bureau (Party B) entered into an Agreement on Leasing of Jixian Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Factory by Hebei Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Co., Ltd., stipulating: Party A shall lease Party B's Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Factory. Party B shall not bear any operational losses or risks. The lease term was ten years (starting from the date of approval of the joint venture company). Party A had the creditor's rights of Jizhou Zhongyi and simultaneously assumed all debts of the original Jizhou Zhongyi before the joint venture.

The document "Current Status of Hebei Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Co., Ltd." issued by Hebei Zhongyi stated: Hebei Zhongyi was signed in Shijiazhuang on September 3, 1992, and was established by three parties, namely, Hebei Provincial Township Enterprise Economic and Trade Development Co., Ltd. (Party A), Jizhou Zhongyi (Party B), and Italy's Sapras Group (Party C). The registered capital was USD 10 million. The loan of USD 1.82 million borrowed by Jizhou Zhongyi, after the Provincial Construction Bank failed to obtain repayment of principal and interest from Jizhou Zhongyi, the Provincial Construction Bank wanted Hebei Zhongyi to take over this loan of USD 1.82 million, i.e., to change the borrower. After several rounds of coordination, Zhonga Company not only did not want to change the guarantor but also wanted to withdraw from its guaranty liability for Jizhou Zhongyi, so the transfer of the loan was not accomplished. To this end, upon the strong suggestion of the Provincial Construction Bank, Hebei Zhongyi undertook in 1995 that Hebei Zhongyi would bear unconditional repayment liability for the principal and interest of this loan and waive all rights of defense. The document "Explanation on Transferring the USD 1.82 Million Loan to Shijiazhuang Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Co., Ltd." issued by Hebei Zhongyi stated: The loan of USD 1.82 million from the Provincial Construction Bank recorded on your factory's accounts was, in the early stage of your factory's lease, handled by Shijiazhuang Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Co., Ltd. on your behalf and borrowed in your factory's name, thus recorded on your factory's accounts. However, according to the written undertaking made by Shijiazhuang Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Co., Ltd. to the Provincial Construction Bank at the time of the loan, the repayment of this loan and interest was not to be borne by your factory but by Shijiazhuang Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Co., Ltd. This loan has no relation to your factory, so please transfer this loan and corresponding interest back.

The Hebei High People's Court held in its trial that the loan contract signed between the Provincial Construction Bank and the defendant Jizhou Zhongyi reflected genuine intentions, was complete in form, and its content did not violate the mandatory provisions of Chinese laws and regulations, so it was lawful and valid. The Irrevocable Foreign Exchange Guaranty Letter issued by the defendant Zhonga Company was its genuine intention, and its capacity as a guarantor was lawful. According to relevant judicial interpretations, it should be determined that the guaranty contract was established and effective. The guaranty letter did not clearly specify the form of guaranty liability, but based on the undertaking in the guaranty letter, the condition for the guarantor to assume liability was when the guaranteed party "fails to repay on time," so it should be determined that the guarantor Zhonga Company assumed joint and several guaranty liability.

During the performance of the loan contract, Hebei Zhongyi, the Provincial Construction Bank, and Zhonga Company negotiated regarding the change of the borrower, but the negotiation failed because Zhonga Company refused to guarantee. In this situation, Hebei Zhongyi undertook to the Provincial Construction Bank that it would bear joint and several repayment liability for the principal and interest of this loan and waive all rights of defense. According to the content of the letter of undertaking, Hebei Zhongyi provided a guaranty to the Provincial Construction Bank for Jizhou Zhongyi's loan, and the Provincial Construction Bank accepted it. Jizhou Zhongyi and Zhonga Company's assertion, based on a different letter of undertaking held by Hebei Zhongyi, that the debt had been transferred to Hebei Zhongyi could not be sustained. The nature of the legal act should be determined based on the content of the letter of undertaking accepted by the creditor Provincial Construction Bank. What Hebei Zhongyi assumed should be a guaranty liability. Zhonga Company refused to provide guaranty for the transferred debt. After Hebei Zhongyi issued the letter of undertaking, the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban only claimed rights against Hebei Zhongyi. On this basis, it could be determined that the guarantor of the loan had been changed to Hebei Zhongyi, and the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban had waived their guaranty rights against Zhonga Company. Therefore, Zhonga Company should no longer bear the guaranty liability in this case. Since the plaintiff Xinda Shiban did not agree to add Hebei Zhongyi as a defendant, the court did not address whether Hebei Zhongyi should bear liability. At the same time, the court rejected the appraisal application filed by Zhonga Company.

The assignment contract of creditor's rights between the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban was lawful and valid, and Xinda Shiban had the standing as plaintiff. From 1998 to 2004, the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban made multiple demands, so the statute of limitations had not expired when the plaintiff filed the lawsuit.

The loan was borrowed in the name of Jizhou Zhongyi and used as equity investment in Hebei Zhongyi's project. Jizhou Zhongyi enjoyed the shareholder rights arising from that investment. This loan was not a loan incurred by the lessee during the lease term. Therefore, the repayment obligation should be borne by Jizhou Zhongyi, the user and beneficiary. The repayment liability was not affected by the adjustment of the project between Jizhou Zhongyi and Hebei Zhongyi.

In summary, Xinda Shiban's claims against Jizhou Zhongyi were well-founded and should be supported. Its request that Zhonga Company bear civil liability was not well-founded and should not be supported. In accordance with the relevant laws cited above, Article 111 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of Civil Law), Article 79 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), and Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), the court rendered the following judgment:

1. Jizhou Zhongyi shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, repay to Xinda Shiban the principal of the loan of USD 1.82 million and interest of USD 2,172,656.50 (interest calculated as of September 21, 2004; interest thereafter shall be calculated according to the overdue penalty interest rate prescribed by the People's Bank of China for the same period until the date of full payment);
2. The other claims of the plaintiff Xinda Shiban are rejected.
The case acceptance fee of RMB 87,553 shall be borne by the defendant Jizhou Zhongyi.

Dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Hebei High People's Court, Xinda Shiban appealed to this Court, alleging:

The first instance judgment exempted the appellee Zhonga Company from guaranty liability on the ground that "the guarantor of the loan had been changed to Hebei Zhongyi, and the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban had waived their guaranty rights against Zhonga Company." This finding had no factual or legal basis, violated the provisions of the relevant judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court, and was completely erroneous.

1. The first instance judgment's finding that "during the performance of the loan contract, Hebei Zhongyi, the Provincial Construction Bank, and Zhonga Company negotiated regarding the change of the borrower, but the negotiation failed because Zhonga Company refused to guarantee" had no legal basis. The sole evidence supporting this finding was the document "Current Status of Hebei Zhongyi Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic Co., Ltd.," which was a solitary piece of evidence with defects, and its issuer, Hebei Zhongyi, had an interest in the defendant at first instance, Jizhou Zhongyi. The Provincial Construction Bank never negotiated with any party regarding the change of the borrower; it only sought to increase the security by adding Hebei Zhongyi as a guarantor. This did not imply the waiver of its guaranty rights against the appellee Zhonga Company.

2. The first instance judgment's finding that "the guarantor of the loan had been changed to Hebei Zhongyi, and the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Company had waived their guaranty rights against Zhonga Company" had no factual basis. There was no clear expression of intention by the Provincial Construction Bank to agree to change or discharge the appellee's guaranty liability, and there was no direct evidence. Moreover, the defendant at first instance, Jizhou Zhongyi, and the appellee Zhonga Company had asserted "debt transfer" in the original trial but never raised the defense of change of guarantor. The court of first instance did not make it a focus of court investigation or conduct cross-examination. The court of first instance arbitrarily used a reason not subject to court investigation and adequate cross-examination to determine the key facts of the case, which clearly violated statutory procedures.

3. The first instance judgment's determination that the Provincial Construction Bank and the appellant had "waived their guaranty rights against Zhonga Company" based on the fact that they did not claim rights against the appellee Zhonga Company seriously violated the provisions of Supreme People's Court Notice Fa (2002) No. 144.

4. After Hebei Zhongyi issued the letter of undertaking, neither the Provincial Construction Bank nor Xinda Shiban waived their guaranty rights against the appellee Zhonga Company. The appellant requests that, on the basis of the facts as ascertained, the second instance court amend the judgment to order the appellee Zhonga Company to bear joint and several repayment liability for the principal and interest of the USD 1.82 million loan of Jizhou Zhongyi, so as to protect the lawful rights and interests of the appellant.

The appellee Zhonga Company responded:

1. The appellant's assertion that "the first instance judgment's determination that the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban had waived their guaranty rights against Zhonga Company had no factual or legal basis" was unfounded. The Provincial Construction Bank never claimed any rights against the respondent. The first instance judgment's finding that "the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban had waived their guaranty rights against Zhonga Company" was based on sufficient and direct evidence. However, the respondent insisted that the Letter of Undertaking issued by Hebei Zhongyi to the Provincial Construction Bank constituted an assignment of creditor's rights. Given the outcome of the first instance judgment, the respondent no longer objects to that finding.

2. The appellant's assertion that the first instance judgment "seriously violated the provisions of Supreme People's Court Notice Fa (2002) No. 144" was incorrect. Moreover, the notarized demand referred to by the appellant never reached the respondent. The conditions for applying Supreme People's Court Notice Fa (2002) No. 144 to the respondent were not met, because the prerequisite for applying the notice is the existence of a legal relationship of debt between the creditor and the counterparty. The first instance judgment determined that the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban had waived their guaranty rights against Zhonga Company. That is, what the appellant acquired from the Provincial Construction Bank was creditor's rights against Jizhou Zhongyi and Hebei Zhongyi, and the respondent had no corresponding debt relationship with the appellant. Therefore, the appellant's reliance on the relevant provisions of Supreme People's Court Notice Fa (2002) No. 144 and Judicial Interpretation Fa Shi (2001) No. 12 was inappropriate and could not serve as a basis for claiming rights against the respondent. Furthermore, the respondent never received the so-called notarized demand notice delivered on November 19, 2002. The notarial certificate proved that the Finance Department of Zhonga Company never had a person named "Han Kejian" (the signatory). As for the appellant's assertion that "the Provincial Construction Bank made multiple demands to the appellee Zhonga Company," that was unfounded. In summary, the first instance judgment's determination that the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban had waived their guaranty rights against Zhonga Company was correct in fact and evidence. The appellant and the respondent had no corresponding debt relationship. The respondent requests that the court reject Xinda Shiban's claims against Zhonga Company.

The defendant at first instance, Jizhou Zhongyi, stated:

1. We do not accept the first instance judgment, but because Jizhou Zhongyi had already gone bankrupt at the time of receiving the first instance judgment, we were unable to appeal.
2. We believe that because the debt of USD 1.82 million had been transferred, the true debtor should be Hebei Zhongyi. The unconditional repayment agreement proposed by Hebei Zhongyi was the most effective, and the letter of undertaking provided by Xinda Shiban was a retraction of Hebei Zhongyi's undertaking.
3. The new evidence submitted by Xinda Shiban just received indicates that Jizhou Zhongyi no longer needs to bear this debt.

Upon retrial by this Court, in addition to confirming the facts found by the original trial, the following facts were also found:

The notarial certificate (2002) Qin Zheng Jing Zi No. 3791 issued on November 19, 2002, by Qinhuangdao Notary Public Office of Hebei Province, submitted by Xinda Shiban to this Court, was verified and found to be consistent with the original copy. Its content is as follows: Pursuant to the Notice of Assignment of Security Rights (Jian Ji Wai No. 4), upon the application of China Xinda Asset Management Corporation Shijiazhuang Office, this notary public office and notary Wang Jiaming, together with Business Manager Gong Jianfeng of China Xinda Asset Management Corporation Shijiazhuang Office, on November 19, 2002, delivered the Notice of Demand for Guaranty Rights to Han Kejian, the head of the Finance Department of the guarantor China-Arab Fertilizer Co., Ltd., and requested the above-mentioned recipient to sign and affix a seal on the notice, which was refused. Accordingly, this notarial certificate confirms that the Notice of Demand for Guaranty Rights was indeed served on the guarantor China-Arab Fertilizer Co., Ltd.

The notarial certificate (2005) Qin San Zheng Min Zi No. 969 submitted by Zhonga Company has the following content: On June 2, 2005, Qinhuangdao Third Notary Public Office notarized the employee register of Zhonga Company for the years 2001 to 2003. The Finance Department of Zhonga Company never had a person named "Han Kejian" (the signatory).

This Court, upon trial, holds:

This case concerns a dispute over a loan guaranty contract. The loan contract signed between the Provincial Construction Bank and Jizhou Zhongyi, and the Irrevocable Guaranty Letter issued by Zhonga Company, were the true intentions of the parties, complete in form, and their content did not violate the mandatory provisions of Chinese laws and regulations. They should be deemed lawful and valid. The guaranty letter did not clearly specify the form of guaranty liability, but according to its content, the condition for the guarantor to assume guaranty liability was when the borrower "fails to repay on time." Pursuant to Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Reply on Issues Concerning the Application of Judicial Interpretations in Guaranty Dispute Cases and the Determination of the Form of Guaranty Liability (Fa Shi [2002] No. 38), "Where a guaranty contract clearly stipulates that the guarantor shall assume guaranty liability when the guaranteed person fails to perform the debt, and the parties' intent cannot be inferred from the terms of the contract to be a general suretyship, it shall be deemed as joint and several suretyship." Therefore, the original trial judgment's determination that the guarantor assumed joint and several suretyship was not improper.

In this case, Hebei Zhongyi, in the "Letter of Commitment" issued to the Provincial Construction Bank, undertook to assume joint and several repayment liability for the repayment of the principal and interest of the loan and to waive all rights of defense. This Letter of Commitment has the same legal effect as the Foreign Exchange Loan Contract No. 93008. Based on this Letter of Commitment, the first-instance judgment found that the guarantor for the loan had been changed to Hebei Zhongyi, and that the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban Office had waived their guaranteed claims against China-Arab, and therefore China-Arab should no longer bear the suretyship liability in this case. However, pursuant to Articles 85 and 91 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, a suretyship contract is a result of mutual agreement between the parties, and a change of guarantor requires the consent of the creditor. Even if the debtor or a third party provides alternative corresponding surety for the creditor and the creditor indicates acceptance of such surety, the suretyship liability is not discharged unless there is an expression of intent between the creditor and the guarantor to extinguish the suretyship liability. In this case, there was no clear expression of intent by the creditor, the Provincial Construction Bank or Xinda Shiban Office, to agree to change or discharge the suretyship liability of China-Arab. Therefore, this finding by the first-instance judgment is clearly a misapprehension of the facts and an erroneous application of law, and should be corrected. Moreover, neither party claimed a change of guarantor, nor did the first-instance court treat the issue of whether the guarantor had changed as a key point of court investigation. Neither party presented evidence or conducted cross-examination on this issue during the trial. It is clearly improper for the first-instance court to use this as the key to determining the facts of the case. The appellant's ground of appeal on this point is supported by this Court.

Based on the content of the Letter of Commitment, there is no doubt that Hebei Zhongyi was willing to assume the debt. The crucial issue is: whether the act of Hebei Zhongyi issuing the Letter of Commitment constitutes a change of debtor, as claimed by the appellee China-Arab, or an addition of a guarantor, as claimed by the appellant Xinda Shiban Office, or a joinder of a new debtor. Pursuant to Article 84 of the Contract Law: "If a debtor transfers all or part of its obligations under a contract to a third party, the consent of the creditor is required as a prerequisite." In this case, Hebei Zhongyi expressed its willingness to assume joint and several repayment liability. While the creditor, the Provincial Construction Bank, accepted this, it did not clearly express its intent to agree to change the debtor from Jizhou Zhongyi to Hebei Zhongyi. Therefore, Hebei Zhongyi's act of commitment cannot constitute a transfer of debt, i.e., it cannot constitute a change of debtor. The appellee China-Arab's defense that it refused to bear suretyship liability on the ground that the debt transfer was not consented to by it is not supported by this Court. As to whether Hebei Zhongyi's act should be characterized as addition of a guarantor, as claimed by the appellant Xinda Shiban Office, or as addition of a debtor, this Court holds that there is no substantive difference in the ultimate handling of the case between the two; the difference lies only in nature: suretyship is an accessory contract, the guarantor is a secondary debtor, and is liable for another's debt; concurrent assumption of debt is an independent contract, the assuming party is one of the principal debtors, and is liable for its own debt, and also represents an increase from a single debtor to two or more joint debtors. Whether an act constitutes suretyship or concurrent assumption of debt should be determined based on the specific circumstances. If the expression of intent to assume the debt contains relatively clear elements of suretyship, it may be identified as suretyship; if not, it should be identified as concurrent assumption of debt, from the legislative purpose of protecting the interests of the creditor. Therefore, in this case, based on the specific content of the Letter of Commitment and the identification of guarantor status in the collection notice sent to Hebei Zhongyi, there is a relatively clear expression and recognition of Hebei Zhongyi's status as a guarantor. The appellant Xinda Shiban Office's ground of appeal that this act constitutes addition of a guarantor is legally sound and is supported by this Court.

Pursuant to Article 6 of this Court's Fa Shi (2001) No. 12 "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving the Acquisition, Management, and Disposition of Assets Formed by Non-Performing Loans of State-Owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies", "After a financial asset management company has acquired a creditor's right from a state-owned bank, if the original creditor bank publishes a notice of the assignment of the creditor's right or notifies the debtor in a nationally or provincially influential newspaper, the people's court may find that the creditor has fulfilled its notification obligation under the Contract Law. In the trial of a case, if the debtor defends on the ground that the original creditor bank failed to perform its notification obligation when assigning the creditor's right, the people's court may summon the original creditor bank to court to investigate the facts of the creditor's right assignment and order the original creditor bank to inform the debtor of the fact of the creditor's right assignment." The Provincial Construction Bank and the appellant Xinda Shiban Office separately asserted their rights against the appellee China-Arab by means of notarized collection on November 19, 2002, and by means of newspaper announcement collection on April 2, 2004. According to this provision, even if the Provincial Construction Bank and the appellant Xinda Shiban Office did not notify China-Arab of the creditor's right assignment, the court could summon the original creditor bank and order it to inform the appellee China-Arab of the creditor's right assignment in court. Therefore, the appellee China-Arab's claim that it refused to bear suretyship liability on the ground that the notice of creditor's right assignment was not served cannot stand. The appellant's ground of appeal that it did not waive its guaranteed claim against the appellee China-Arab is supported by this Court. Regarding the appellee China-Arab's challenge to the method of collection, according to Article 67 of the Civil Procedure Law and Article 9(6) of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedures, the notarized collection method has legal effect and can produce the effect prescribed by law. The appellant Xinda Shiban Office submitted a copy of the Notarial Certificate (2002) Qinzheng Jing Zi No. 3791. After verification with the original, the content of the notarized service of the creditor's right collection document is true, and the expression of intent is clear. This Court affirms its validity. China-Arab's claim that the social insurance records for its employees did not include Han Kejian was provided after the fact. Whether or not the company actually had an employee named Han Kejian does not affect the truthfulness and validity of the notarial service. Therefore, the evidence of the social insurance list submitted by China-Arab cannot counter the probative force of the Notarial Certificate (2002) Qinzheng Jing Zi No. 3791 issued by the Notary Public Office of Qinhuangdao City, Hebei Province on November 19, 2002. China-Arab's defense is not accepted by this Court.

The loan contract in this case was signed before the effectiveness of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Guarantee Law). If there were no provisions in the laws and regulations at that time, the Guarantee Law could be applied by reference. However, where the provisions of the Guarantee Law are inconsistent with the laws and regulations in effect at that time, the provisions of the laws and regulations in effect at the time of the contract's signing and performance should apply. Therefore, this case should apply the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning Suretyship in Economic Contract Dispute Cases" promulgated in 1994. At the same time, this Court's Notice (2002) No. 144 should also serve as one of the legal bases for handling this case. Pursuant to Articles 11 and 29 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning Suretyship in Economic Contract Dispute Cases promulgated in 1994, for a suretyship contract without a specified surety period or with an unclear surety period, the guarantor shall bear suretyship liability within the period during which the guaranteed person bears liability. The suspension of the statute of limitations for the principal debt also suspends the statute of limitations for the guaranteed debt. The Provincial Construction Bank's collection against Jizhou Zhongyi on July 8, 1998, produced the legal effect of suspending the statute of limitations for the principal debtor Jizhou Zhongyi and also produced the legal effect of suspending the statute of limitations for the guaranteed debt of the guarantor China-Arab. Subsequently, pursuant to this Court's Notice (2002) No. 144, which provides: "For a suretyship contract signed before the effectiveness of the Guarantee Law without a specified surety period or with an unclear surety period, if the creditor has already asserted its rights against the principal debtor within the statutory limitation period, such that the principal debt has not exceeded the limitation period, but has not asserted its rights against the guarantor, the creditor may assert its rights against the guarantor within six months from the date of issuance of this Notice. If it fails to do so within that period, the guarantor shall no longer bear liability." The appellant Xinda Shiban Office, within six months from the date of issuance of this Notice, i.e., within the six-month period from August 1, 2002, to January 31, 2003, conducted a collection against China-Arab by notarization in November 2002, thereby suspending the statute of limitations for the guaranteed claim. Subsequently, on April 2, 2004, the appellant Xinda Shiban Office published a collection announcement against Jizhou Zhongyi and China-Arab in the Hebei Economic Daily, again suspending the statute of limitations for the guaranteed claim. By the time the appellant filed the lawsuit, the guaranteed claim against the appellee was still within the statute of limitations. Therefore, the Provincial Construction Bank and the appellant did not waive their guaranteed claim against China-Arab, and their appeal request is supported by this Court.

In summary, the appellant Xinda Shiban Office's request that the appellee China-Arab bear joint and several liability for the repayment of the principal and interest of the USD 1,820,000 loan of Jizhou Zhongyi is reasonable and is supported by this Court. The appellee China-Arab's defenses that, due to the debt transfer, the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban Office had waived their guaranteed claim against China-Arab, so China-Arab no longer bears suretyship liability, and that the appellant's claim had exceeded the statute of limitations, cannot stand and are dismissed by this Court. The original judgment's finding that "the guarantor for the loan had been changed to Hebei Zhongyi, and the Provincial Construction Bank and Xinda Shiban Office had waived their guaranteed claims against China-Arab" and that the appellee China-Arab did not bear suretyship liability constitutes a misapprehension of the facts and an erroneous application of law and should be corrected according to law.

Pursuant to Articles 85 and 91 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 11 and 29 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning Suretyship in Economic Contract Dispute Cases", Article 9(6) of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedures", and Articles 153(1)(1), 153(1)(2), and 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. Sustains Item 1 of the main text of the civil judgment (2005) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 2 of the Hebei High People's Court;

2. Sets aside Item 2 of the main text of the civil judgment (2005) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 2 of the Hebei High People's Court;

3. China-Arab Chemical Fertilizer Co., Ltd. shall bear joint and several liability for the repayment of the principal and interest of the USD 1,820,000 loan of the defendant at first instance, Hebei Jizhou City Zhongyi FRP Factory.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 87,553, to be borne by Hebei Jizhou City Zhongyi FRP Factory; court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 87,553, to be borne by China-Arab Chemical Fertilizer Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
